title: set --findings updates the index row but not the slice file; check does not notice

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
`ops.promote` copies five fields from the index item onto the new slice — title,
findings, size, flags and trees — and from that moment nothing keeps them in step. The
roadmap row renders from `Item`; the slice header renders from `Slice`. So
`slicer set S01 --findings G9` updates the table and leaves the slice saying `G1`, and
`slicer check` does not notice because nothing compares the two.

Found while splitting the repo: the S01 findings note named the parent project, and
fixing it with `set --findings` changed the index while the rendered slice kept the old
text. There was no command that could repair it, so it took a hand edit of
`.slicer/slices/S01.json` — the one thing the tool exists to make unnecessary.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `Set_Findings_UpdatesTheSliceHeaderToo` — set it, then assert `slicer show` renders
   the new value.
2. `Set_Size_UpdatesTheSlice`, `Set_Trees_UpdateTheSliceNoteAndPlural`,
   `Set_Title_UpdatesTheSlice`.
3. `Set_PassKey_DoesNotRewriteTheSliceFile` — an index-only field must not touch it.
4. `Set_OnAnUnpromotedItem_IsStillFine`.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
A private `_sync_slice(state, item)` called from `set_fields` after any relocation,
mapping exactly what `promote` maps: `findings`→`findings_note`, `size`, `trees`→
`trees_note` plus `trees_plural`, `flags`, and `title`. `short_title` has no slice
counterpart and stays index-only, deliberately — the index cell is scannable and the
slice H1 is explicit, and they differ in most real slices.

Skip the write when nothing changed, so `set --pass 2` does not rewrite a slice file for
no reason. Order matters: relocate first, then sync, because `save_slice` derives its
path from the item's status and must write to the file's new home.

**Not in this slice:** reconciling an already-imported tree. `migrate` deliberately
allows the index and the slice to disagree and reports `title / findings / trees
differences - both sides kept`, because a legacy tree legitimately carries a short table
title and a longer slice heading. This syncs on an explicit `set` and nothing else.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
`slicer set S01 --findings X` then `slicer show S01` shows X in the rendered header, and
`slicer check` stays clean.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body:
One commit, after S11 — both land in `set_fields`, and the relocation has to exist
before the sync can run in the right order.
